summary: John Nemec is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania in 2005. Having studied under Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher, he is an Associate Professor at the University of Virginia (attested 2020–2026).

John Okell (1934–2020) was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford (~1954–1958) and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. From 1959 to 1999, he was a research associate at SOAS University of London.

John P. Keenan (b. 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He served as a Research Fellow at Nanzan University (1983–1986) and taught at Middlebury College.

John Peile (1837–1910) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, and under Theodor Benfey. He spent his career at Cambridge as a Fellow and Tutor at Christ's (~1860–1910) and Reader of Comparative Philology (1884–1891).
John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams and held an appointment as Professor at the University of Madras.

John Powers (b. 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed his doctorate at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. His posts include professorships at the Australian National University and Deakin University (2016–2022).

John R. B. Campbell is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, also studying with the 14th Dalai Lama, among other traditional teachers.

John R. McRae (1947–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He held teaching posts at Cornell (~1987–1995), Indiana University Bloomington (~1996–2005), and Komazawa University (~2008–2011).
John Riley Perks is a Buddhist studies figure who studied under the traditional teachers Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

John Ronald Newman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD in 1987 at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

John Ross Carter (1938–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctoral work at Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith. He served as a professor at Colgate University from ~1972 to 2014.

John S. Strong (b. 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Frank E. Reynolds, and later served as Dana Professor Emeritus at Bates College.

John Shakespear (1774–1858) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under John Richardson. He held professorships at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809) and the Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).
John Shore (1751–1834) was an Indologist and historian who succeeded William Jones and served as President of The Asiatic Society from ~1794 to 1798.

John Stratton Hawley (b. 1941) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held a post at Bowdoin College (~1974–1978) before becoming a Professor at Columbia University (~1986).
John Stuart Mill (1806–1873) was a philosopher who studied at University College London (~1828–1830) and worked at the East India Company from ~1823 to 1858.

John Sydenham Furnivall (1878–1960) was a historian who studied at Cambridge and Leiden University. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910 and later held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1948–1953).

John Taber (b. 1948) is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He taught at Case Western Reserve University (~1983–1989) and joined the University of New Mexico (~1989).

John Thompson Platts (1830–1904) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held teaching posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1858–1861) and served as Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford from 1880.

John Vincent Bellezza (b. 1957) is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel. He was affiliated with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
